script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session
tools.description: Move the task you are in the middle of into its own session (a fork of this conversation plus your remaining plan) so you can answer the user now. Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. # Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

## Writing the test

- Name the test case as a plain behavioral sentence in the present tense. No `Subsystem:` prefix.
- Tag it with the subsystem it covers, matching the file, in PascalCase. That tag is what people filter on, so every test needs one.
- Add further tags where they help: a narrower one to slice a large file (`[Rotcalip]`, `[Placer]`), a shared one for something spanning files (`[Python]`, `[H2C]`, `[Regression]`), or `[NotWorking]` / `[.]` to disable or hide a test. Say why in a comment if you disable or hide.
- Prefer a flat `TEST_CASE` per behavior, with `GENERATE` for parameterized cases. Reserve `SCENARIO` / `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` for genuine shared setup that branches into a few close variations.
- Set the config keys your test depends on, and derive the expected values from what you set. A 20mm cube sliced at `layer_height` 2 is 10 layers, and the test should state both parts. If a number in your assertion comes from a key you never set, the test is also testing that default.
- Assert the defining property, not an incidental value. "Skirt present" or "at least 2 brim loops" survives a refactor; exact coordinates and byte counts do not.
- Name a regression test for the behavior it protects, never for an issue or PR number.
- When asserting on G-code, match the meaningful token such as `; skirt` rather than whole lines, whitespace or comment wording. Depend on ordering only when ordering is the contract.

## Catch2 rules that cause real breakage

- Never reuse a `SECTION` name inside a loop. Use `DYNAMIC_SECTION` so each iteration is unique.
- Never assert from a spawned thread. Catch2 assertions are not thread-safe. Collect results in the thread and assert on the main thread.
- Never combine conditions with `&&` or `||` inside one assertion. Split them so Catch2 can print both operands on failure.
- Compare floats with `WithinAbs` or `WithinRel`, never `==`. Prefer these over `Approx` in new tests.
- Keep tests self-contained: no shared state, green under `--order rand`.

## Error handling

Less is more. An error is **expected** only when the person can do something about it, such as sign in again, get more credits, update a key or check the network, and Kenneth decided what the product tells them. Every other error is **unexpected**: the person sees one generic sentence and a way to report the problem, and the report carries everything known, so that we can find the cause.

Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause analysis. And that's it, nothing else." And: "When it comes to error handling, less is more."

The reporting function is `report_unexpected_error` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`). This repository has no expected-errors table yet.

### Expected errors

- Each has an entry in the expected-errors table: the cause, what the person sees, and what they can do next. A new entry needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message.
- The test is what the person can do next. If the answer is "nothing" or only "try again later", the error is unexpected. An AI provider or our own server being slow, overloaded, down or limiting us is unexpected: the person can do nothing about any of them.
- Two causes that leave the person doing the same thing do not get separate sentences, codes or branches.
- A cause is "out of credits" or "no network". A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause.
- Each entry has a test, and each occurrence is counted.
- Handle them with normal control flow, not exceptions.

### Unexpected errors

- Write no code for them. Do not catch one, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own. Each of those is a guess about a failure nobody understands. It hides the failure and loses where it came from.
- Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged.
- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it.
- One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports.
- A tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, its error goes to the AI model, and the turn goes on; no dialog opens. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's mistake, it is also reported, and only if the person has turned automatic reports on.
- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected.
- The report carries as much as is known: the other side's status, request id and error text, and the request's own facts, such as the user, the chat, the turn and the model. The person is told none of it.
- Never record a failure as a success.
- A log line is not a report: it reaches nobody.

### Catching

- Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.

### Checks

- An agent reads the changed code against these rules and asks one question wherever the code decides what happened: can the person do something about it, and did Kenneth decide what they are told?
- Do not sort unexpected failures into kinds for the person, and do not bring Kenneth a question about the wording of a failure the person can do nothing about. On 2026-11-16 the code that kept five "try again" sentences apart was deleted for this reason.
- To audit a commit range, use the `error-handling` skill (`.claude/skills/error-handling/`). To check production for a period, use the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise repository.

# Error-handling sweep: trial findings

This file is the result of a reading-only sweep. It checks JusPrin's AI chat and Home code, and the JusPrin Cloud server's v2 code, against the trial copy of the error-handling rules and the `error-handling` audit skill. Nothing was built, run, changed or committed.

What was read:
- **Desktop app:** every `.cpp`/`.hpp` under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` and `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/` at commit `5e173c5e15`.
- **Server:** every `.py` under `web_ent/jusprin/v2/` except `tests/` and `migrations/`, at `2086b2ec64` in tsd-enterprise.

How it was judged:
- An outcome counts as decided by a person only if its cause is in `expected-errors-app.cpp` or `expected-errors-server.py`.
- Every other outcome counts as an unexpected error.

How to read the locations:
- Line numbers are from those two commits.
- App paths start at `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Server paths start at `web_ent/jusprin/v2/`.
- "Confirmed" means I read the code myself. Several findings were first reported by a reader subagent and then confirmed by me.
- Nothing was confirmed by running code.

## 1. Findings, most harmful first

### 1. In the desktop app, no failure is ever reported, and a thrown one reaches OrcaSlicer's generic handler
- **Where:**
  - The entry-point handler is `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:926-947` (`on_page_message`). It catches `json::exception`, adds the message type and id, and rethrows. That part is allowed.
  - The rethrow, and every other throw from the chat page, the timer pumps, Home's page messages (`Home/HomeHost.cpp:161`), Home's `CallAfter` bodies (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:749`, `:769-785`, `:851-863`, `:1371-1378`) and the tool pump (`ShellController.cpp:337-339`, which has no try), all end in `GUI_App::OnExceptionInMainLoop` → `generic_exception_handle` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:855-909`, `:9600-9604`).
  - Nothing in Agent/ or Home/ calls a reporting function.
- **What the code does:** OrcaSlicer's handler writes a log line and queues `wxLogError("OrcaSlicer got an unhandled exception: %1%")` with the exception text, then rethrows with `throw;`. The comment at `AgentHost.cpp:931-934` says this handler "logs it and reports it once". It does not report.
- **Rule broken:** "One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports."
- **What goes wrong:** Someone hits a bug, for example a page message missing a field, or Home asking for an unknown sign-in link (`OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:740`). They see an Orca-branded error that holds internal text such as "jusprin-agent-bridge: … ". Nothing reaches JusPrin. My inference, not run: because the handler rethrows, the app then quits.
- **Confidence:** high for the missing handler and report. Medium that the app quits.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 2. A model list whose shape changes crashes the app, because parsing throws on OrcaSlicer's HTTP thread
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:43-62`: `on_complete` calls `parse_model_list`.
  - `Agent/ModelCatalog.cpp:177-188`: it reads `response.at("data")`, `model.at("id").get<std::string>()`, `model.at("format")` and `model.at("credits").get<int>()`.
  - `src/slic3r/Utils/Http.cpp:796-801`: `perform()` runs `http_perform` on a `std::thread`. At `:519-526` that thread calls `completefn` directly, with no try around it.
- **What the code does:** If one model entry has no `format`, or its `credits` is not an integer, a `json` exception leaves a `std::thread` body. That calls `std::terminate`.
- **Rule broken:** "One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure…". The HTTP callback is an entry point with no handler. Keeping the parser strict is right; what is missing is the handler at the top.
- **What goes wrong:** One field changed on JusPrin Cloud, or in a provider's model list, makes the app quit each time it fetches models. That happens at launch and at sign-in. Nothing is reported.
- **Confidence:** high, by reading.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 3. An AI-request status the table does not name is shown as a network problem, and every 5xx as "temporarily unavailable"
- **Where:** `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:667-699` (`http_error`).
- **What the code does:** It sorts statuses by fixed rules and ends in `network_error`, "The AI request could not reach the … service.", with Retry. That last line catches:
  - 400, 404, 405, 409, 410 and 422;
  - 402 from any provider other than JusPrin's account;
  - any status other than 408 that came with no curl text.

  Any status of 500 or above other than 529 becomes `service_unavailable`. That includes JusPrin Cloud's own 502 `upstream_error` and 500 tracebacks. Because the `>= 500` test comes before the timeout test, the gateway's 504 `timeout` never becomes `timeout`. A 402 from JusPrin Cloud that is not `credits_exhausted` still becomes "You're out of credits." (`:683-685`). 401 and 403 always mean the sign-in ended or the key was rejected (`:673-674`, `:686-687`).
- **Rules broken:**
  - "A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause."
  - "Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it."
  - "When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected."
- **What goes wrong:**
  - JusPrin Cloud refuses the app's own request with 400 `invalid_request`, which is a bug on one of our two ends. The person is told to check their network and Retry, which never helps. Nobody hears of it.
  - Someone's OpenAI key cannot use the model they typed, and OpenAI answers 404. They get the same network sentence. Key setup takes the same path (`Agent/AgentSetup.cpp:112-127`).
  - A gateway fault reads as a provider outage.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 4. An error event inside the reply stream loses its code, so even causes the table names are shown as a generic failure
- **Where:** `Agent/ResponsesCodec.cpp:176-177` and `Agent/AnthropicCodec.cpp:404-405`. Both turn any `error` or `response.failed` event into `agent_service_error`, "The AI service could not complete the response.", and drop the event's code and message.
- **Related:** `Agent/AnthropicCodec.cpp:413-428`. `max_tokens` and `model_context_window_exceeded` become Incomplete. A stop reason this build does not know gets the invented sentence "ended its response for a reason this build does not know".
- **Rules broken:** "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own."
- **What goes wrong:** These failures, three of which have table entries, show as the same generic line with Retry:
  - Anthropic's mid-stream `overloaded_error` (table: `service_overloaded`);
  - the gateway's own mid-stream `timeout` (table: `timeout`);
  - the gateway's `upstream_error` (a gateway fault that should be reported).

  The saved message keeps only `agent_service_error`.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 5. Server: a reply that ends with the provider's own error event is recorded as completed, and its chat is kept as completed
- **Where:**
  - `gateway.py:301-307`: `self.outcome = 'completed'` is set whenever the upstream line iterator ends, whatever the last event was.
  - `stream.py:49-52` (Anthropic) and `:67-73` (Responses): an upstream `error` event, or a `response.error`, is rewritten to `STREAM_ERROR_MESSAGE` and forwarded, and the loop carries on.
  - `stream.py:100-109`: an unterminated last event is dropped without a word.
  - `gateway.py:241`: `keep()` then keeps the chat for fine-tuning as a completed reply.
  - `_log` (`gateway.py:330-361`) records outcome `completed` in Langfuse.
  - Nothing reports it.
- **Rules broken:** "Never record a failure as a success." "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own." (The sentence is "The model service failed while answering.")
- **What goes wrong:** When a provider fails mid-reply, the person sees a failure. The Langfuse record says completed. The kept chat, which is training data, holds a failed reply marked as complete. Nobody can count these failures.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 6. Server: upstream refusals are interpreted and given sentences of their own; only 401, 403 and 404 reach Sentry, and the provider's error text is dropped
- **Where:**
  - `upstream.py:197-208` (`error_for_status`): 400 and 422 become `invalid_request`, "The model service did not accept the request." Any other 4xx becomes `upstream_error` 502. Every status of 500 or above becomes `unavailable`.
  - `gateway.py:320-328` (`_upstream_failed`): Sentry is told only for `is_gateway_fault` statuses (401, 403 and 404, `upstream.py:211-214`). Everything else is `logger.warning`.
  - `gateway.py:312-315`: a transport error mid-stream sends an `upstream_error` event. It too is only a warning.
  - `gateway.py:321` drops the upstream body on purpose ("an upstream body can echo the prompt"). The client never receives the upstream status.
- **Rules broken:**
  - "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it."
  - "A log line is not a report: it reaches nobody."
  - "No other code reports." Sentry is called at the failure site, not in a top handler.
- **What goes wrong:** The provider starts refusing the gateway's requests with 400, for example after a model id or field changes. Every person's chat fails, and the app then calls it a network problem (finding 3). The server has only warning lines, with no provider text explaining why.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 7. Server: no endpoint has a top handler that reports and says "Something went wrong on our side"
- **Where:**
  - `gateway.py:136-185`: `_handle_in` catches only `GatewayError`. Anything else leaves `GatewayEndpoint.asgi` (`:117-130`) for daphne. That includes `ImproperlyConfigured` for a missing provider key (`upstream.py:185-187`), Redis or ledger errors in `admit` (`credits.py`), `remember_chat_title`, and an exception in `EventRewriter` mid-stream.
  - The Django views (`views.py`, `web.py`, `sign_in.py`) rely on Django's default 500.
  - `report_unexpected` does not exist at this commit.
- **Rule broken:** "One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side"…"
- **What goes wrong:**
  - Before the reply starts, the app gets daphne's plain-text 500. The app then shows "temporarily unavailable" (finding 3).
  - After the 200, the stream just stops.
  - Whether Sentry sees these depends on the Sentry SDK's logging integration catching daphne's error log line. I did not check that.
- **Confidence:** high for the missing handler. Unverified whether Sentry sees it.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 8. A project's chat state that fails to save is marked saved, and one that fails to read is overwritten with an empty one
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/ProjectPersistence.cpp:495-498`: `write_state_to` ignores `write_file`'s `false`.
  - `:400-401`: `flush` sets `m_dirty = false` anyway.
  - `:44-60`: `write_file` ignores `create_directories`' error code.
  - `:34-42`: `read_file` returns `{}` when the file cannot be opened, for any reason.
  - `:302-306`: `adopt_current_project` reads empty as "no state yet" and calls `start_fresh_identity`. That flushes a new document over the same `state.json` (in the non-managed case, `state_file_path()` and `write_state_to(jusprin_data_dir())` are the same file).
  - `:308-317`: a corrupt `state.json`, or one from a newer build, is renamed to `.corrupt`/`.newer` (the rename's error is ignored) and a fresh chat history starts. Nobody is told. The managed path (`:410-413`) throws `NewerFormatError` instead.
- **Rules broken:**
  - "Never record a failure as a success."
  - "A failure that arrives as a value … Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop."
  - "Do not … give it a default value."
  - "When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected."
- **What goes wrong:**
  - Someone's disk is full. Their chat looks fine, but none of it was saved, and the next open starts empty.
  - A transient read failure, such as a permissions change or a locked file, wipes the saved chats of a project opened from a folder.
  - None of this is reported.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 9. Attachments drop out of the request to the AI, or are sent empty, while the person sees them sent
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:1371-1378`: attachment ids that are unknown or not `staged` are "dropped rather than trusted". The ids come from our own page.
  - `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:3161-3178`: a text, G-code, SVG, image or PDF attachment whose file is missing or unreadable reads as an empty string (`ProjectPersistence::read_attachment_blob`, `ProjectPersistence.cpp:532-543`, returns `{}`). That empty content goes to the model. The same condition throws in `load_record_text` (`AgentHost.cpp:3023-3025`).
  - `Agent/ImageThumbnail.cpp:35-36`, `:49-50`: an image wx cannot decode, or cannot re-encode, returns nullopt. `AgentHost.cpp:3174-3178` then sends the original bytes.
- **Rules broken:** "Do not … give it a default value." "Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged." "When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected."
- **What goes wrong:** Someone attaches a photo of a failed print. The model answers as if there were no photo, or describes an empty file. Nobody is told.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 10. When the chat document cannot be saved, the person gets invented sentences, and two save results are ignored
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:2196-2213` (`checkpoint_active_chat`): the pin, the checkpoint save and the document save each return only a bool or optional, so the reason is gone.
  - `:2241-2245`: "The new chat could not be saved."
  - `:2331-2339`: "The current project could not be saved before restoration." and "JusPrin couldn't put the project back.", which then blocks the chat.
  - `:2342`: after a restore, the result of `checkpoint_active_chat()` is thrown away.
  - `:2237`: `save_chat_checkpoint`'s result for the new chat is ignored.
- **Rules broken:** "Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's … error text." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own." "Never record a failure as a success."
- **What goes wrong:** A failed save after a restore goes unnoticed, while the chat says "Restored this chat's saved project setup." Other save failures show a vague line, and nobody can learn why.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 11. A key or sign-in that fails to save is shown as verified with a warning, and sign-in failures collapse into "Try again"
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:2787-2799`: `m_setup->commit` fails, the warning "This key could not be saved…" is set, and the status is still `verified`.
  - `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:660-662` does the same for a sign-in.
  - `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:285-297` (`answered`):
    - any 400 to `login` that is not `too_many_login_attempts` becomes `wrong_password`;
    - any 409 on `code/confirm` becomes `expired_code`;
    - everything else becomes "JusPrin couldn't sign you in. Try again."
  - `:323-324`: any failed browser sign-in becomes "Signing in didn't finish. Nothing was saved. Try again." The authorization's own error is ignored.
  - `:359-361`: any non-200 or unreadable answer from `me` or `models` becomes "JusPrin couldn't be reached to finish signing in."
  - `:378-380`: a model format this build cannot build an agent for becomes "JusPrin has no AI model for this account right now."
  - `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:668-673` repeats these sentences for Home.
- **Rules broken:** "Never record a failure as a success." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own." "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text." "When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected."
- **What goes wrong:**
  - A server 500 during sign-in says "Try again" forever, with no report.
  - A typo in an email address is called a wrong password.
  - A key that seemed saved is gone at the next launch.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 12. A failure inside the app during a tool call goes back to the model as data and is never reported; a failed project save around a call is caught and logged
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:63-84` maps `WorkspaceError::Failed` to `"failed"` and `Refused` to `"refused"`. That mapping is used at about 25 call sites.
  - `fail()` (`:2508-2531`) records the failure, and `AgentHost::continue_after_tool` sends it to the model.
  - `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp:5-28` is the policy: "Stop and tell the person".
  - `:1148-1154` and `:1179-1196`: a failed save before or after a call is caught as `std::exception`, written to `std::clog`, and made into a tool failure with its own sentence ("Nothing ran: the project could not be saved first…", "The change was made, but the project could not be saved…").
  - `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:663-667`: a failed tool call is a log warning only.
- **Rules broken:**
  - "Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged."
  - "One handler at the top of each entry point reports…"
  - "Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow."
  - "A log line is not a report."
- **What goes wrong:** An export fails because the disk is full. The person reads whatever the model says about it, and nothing reaches JusPrin. The save catch also swallows bugs, and words them as "could not be saved".
- **Confidence:** high that this conflicts with the rules as written. It is unsettled whether a tool result counts as "telling the person" (see part 3).
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 13. A tool reports a failed slice cancel as success, and a slice that did not start gets an invented reason
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1802-1805`: `m_workspace.cancel_slice(cancelled)` returns a `CommandResult`, which is discarded. When it fails, the call succeeds with "Nothing was stopped. The tools stop only a slice they started.", which is false for a slice the tools did start.

- **Rules broken:** "A failure that arrives as a value … Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop." "Never record a failure as a success." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own."
- **What goes wrong:** Someone asks the AI to stop a slice. The slice keeps running, and the model tells them the slice was not one it started.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 14. Messages from our own code that the other side refuses are answered with sentences of their own and never reported (app bridge and server)
- **App:** `Agent/AgentHost.cpp` answers the chat page with `bridge_error` codes, and the page shows `payload.message`. Examples:
  - `unknown_type` at 1072-1073;
  - `invalid_payload` at 1063-1064, 1114-1116 and five more places;
  - `stale_conversation`, `invalid_retry`, `unknown_action`, `invalid_transition`, `rename_failed` and `unsupported`, at about 40 sites in all. The full list is in the reader's report.
- **Home:** `Home/HomeHost.cpp:163-171` drops a page message that is not JSON. The comment calls this "a bug in the page".
- **Server:** these refusals go out with no report and no log line:

  - `upstream.py:58`, `:60`, `:63`, `:67`, `:70`, `:72`, `:100`, `:105`, `:123`, `:131`, `:144`;
  - `views.py:165`, `:167`, `:253`, `:255`.

  Each carries a specific sentence ("The X-JusPrin-Turn header is missing or not valid.", "Field "x" is not allowed.").
- **Rules broken:** "When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own." "No other code reports." The server table lists `invalid_request`, `unknown_model` and `method_not_allowed` as unexpected.
- **What goes wrong:** When the app and the server, or the page and the host, fall out of step after a release, people see odd specific lines or clicks that do nothing. Nobody can see it happening.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes. I read a sample of the app sites and every server site.

- **Rules broken:** "Do not … give it a default value." "Never record a failure as a success." "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text."
- **What goes wrong:** When the account endpoint is failing, the person sees a stale credit balance, or none, with no word. The app reports nothing.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes for AgentHost, ModelCatalogFetch `:64-72` and OrcaHomeBackend. The account-box line numbers are the reader's.

### 16. Home's print report: the server's answer is reduced to "failed", and the report is shown as sent when it was not recorded
- **Where:**
  - `Home/PrintHistory.cpp:181-197`: any answer other than 201 with an object, 409 `already_reported` or `update_required` becomes Failed, with no status or body kept. A 201 that cannot be parsed also becomes Failed, although the server stored the report. A missing `credits` becomes 0.
  - `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1367-1370`: only a warning holding the status is written.
  - `:1392`: `on_error` drops curl's error text.
  - `:1374-1377`: with no shell, the report is not recorded, but `done(answer)` still tells the page it was sent.
- **Rules broken:** "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text." "A log line is not a report." "Never record a failure as a success."
- **What goes wrong:** Someone's report reaches the server, but Home says it failed. When they retry, they are told it was already sent.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 17. Home: when the projects folder cannot be read, Home shows a sentence of its own and retries every second; an empty Print history then looks real
- **Where:**
  - `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:975-976`: "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying."
  - The retry is the one-second refresh in `Home/HomeHost.cpp:101-122`.
  - `:1229-1234`: `print_history()` calls `recent_projects()` and discards its problem, so Print history shows empty.
  - `:444-450`: an unreadable folder counts as "no projects", so first-run is not skipped.
- **Rules broken:** "Do not … retry it, or give it a sentence of its own." "Let the failure stop the work."
- **What goes wrong:** Someone with a permissions problem sees an empty Print history. Nothing is reported.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 18. Home: a dropped file that is cut short is opened as if whole, and catch blocks turn file-system failures into sentences
- **Where:**
  - `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1454`: the `std::ofstream(...).write(...)` result is never checked. On a full disk the truncated file is hashed and opened.
  - `:1466-1471`: every `std::exception` is caught and becomes "%s couldn't be opened. Try opening it with Open… instead."
  - `:1297-1305`: `filesystem_error` during a G-code export is caught, logged and shown as "The G-code couldn't be written to %s." The comment says "the person picks again", but nothing reopens the dialog.
- **Rules broken:** "Never record a failure as a success." "Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it… and then rethrow." "A log line is not a report."
- **What goes wrong:** A half-written model opens as though it were the dropped file.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 19. Importing another app's printers: a failed profile install is logged and the import goes on, ending in "couldn't load, try again"
- **Where:**
  - `Home/OrcaImporter.cpp:224-226`: `install_printer_profiles` fails. It is logged and the import continues.
  - `:328-341`: each printer then becomes `NotImported`/`NotLoaded`.
  - The sentence at `OrcaImporter.cpp:100-101` tells the person to try again.
- **Rules broken:** "Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged." "A log line is not a report." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own."
- **What goes wrong:** Someone moving from another app gets "try again" for a failure that will happen again. Nothing reaches JusPrin.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 20. Server: Chargebee failures at checkout and cancel are caught and shown as the page's own sentences, with no report
- **Where:**
  - `web.py:254-262`: any `chargebee.APIError` at checkout redirects to prices with `?error=checkout`.
  - `web.py:393-398`: any `APIError` on cancel shows "The plan couldn't be cancelled", then "Nothing changed. Try again in a minute."
  - `web.py:271-273`: `finish_checkout` returning None means a checkout that did not succeed, or one for another account (`ledger/billing.py:322-342`, outside the sweep). The person who just paid lands on the prices page with no word.
- **Rules broken:** "Do not catch one … give it a sentence of its own." "Catch an error only when it is an expected one…" No table entry covers checkout or cancel failures.
- **What goes wrong:** If the Chargebee key or a plan id breaks, every buyer sees a checkout error and nobody at JusPrin knows. "Nothing changed" is a guess.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 21. The app cuts any AI reply that lasts more than 120 seconds and calls it a timeout
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/AgentTransport.hpp:27`: `request_timeout_seconds{120}`.
  - `Agent/OpenAIHttpTransport.cpp:33`: this is passed to `timeout_max`.
  - `src/slic3r/Utils/Http.cpp:334-336`: `timeout_max` sets `CURLOPT_TIMEOUT`, the total transfer time.
  - Classified as `timeout` at `ProviderAgent.cpp:696-697`.
  - The server allows 300 seconds of read silence (`gateway.py:47`).
- **Rule at stake:** The table's `timeout` cause is "took too long to answer, or the connection to it stalled". A reply still streaming is neither, so this is an undecided failure dressed as an expected one.
- **What goes wrong:** A long reply that is still arriving is cut, and the person is told to Retry.
- **Confidence:** medium. Whether replies actually last that long was not measured.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 22. A message from the app to the chat page can be lost without a trace, and it is counted as sent
- **Where:**

  - `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:101-107`: a stored report that does not parse becomes a discarded JSON value inside the envelope. My expectation, not checked: nlohmann prints a discarded value as `<discarded>`, which makes the whole envelope invalid script.
- **Rules broken:** "A failure that arrives as a value … Turn it into a thrown error on the spot." "Do not … give it a default value."
- **What goes wrong:** If `assistant_failed` or `state` never reaches the page, the page waits forever. One corrupt stored report could blank the chat on every reload. That second effect is my inference.

- **Confirmed:** yes for the code. The `<discarded>` output is not checked.

### 23. A chat-titles file that cannot be read is started over, which wipes it, and failed writes are only logged

- **What goes wrong:** Every chat in Account's usage table loses its title, and nobody knows why.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 24. Connecting an outside AI client: every exception is caught, and the code chooses what to say by searching the error text
- **Where:** `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:4152-4170` (`handle_mcp_preview`): any `std::exception`, including a parse failure of our own catalog text, becomes `write_failed` with `what()`, retryable. `:4202-4213` (`handle_mcp_connect`): `stale_preview` or `write_failed` is chosen by `text.find("changed after the preview")`.
- **Rules broken:** "Catch an error only when it is an expected one…" "Do not interpret it."
- **What goes wrong:** A bug shows up as a write error with Retry. Rewording one exception message silently changes what the person is told.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

1	# Error-handling sweep: trial findings
2	
3	This file is the result of a reading-only sweep. It checks JusPrin's AI chat and Home code, and the JusPrin Cloud server's v2 code, against the trial copy of the error-handling rules and the `error-handling` audit skill. Nothing was built, run, changed or committed.
4	
5	What was read:
6	- **Desktop app:** every `.cpp`/`.hpp` under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` and `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/` at commit `5e173c5e15`.
7	- **Server:** every `.py` under `web_ent/jusprin/v2/` except `tests/` and `migrations/`, at `2086b2ec64` in tsd-enterprise.
8	
9	How it was judged:
10	- An outcome counts as decided by a person only if its cause is in `expected-errors-app.cpp` or `expected-errors-server.py`.
11	- Every other outcome counts as an unexpected error.
12	
13	How to read the locations:
14	- Line numbers are from those two commits.
15	- App paths start at `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Server paths start at `web_ent/jusprin/v2/`.
16	- "Confirmed" means I read the code myself. Several findings were first reported by a reader subagent and then confirmed by me.
17	- Nothing was confirmed by running code.
18	
19	## 1. Findings, most harmful first
20	
21	### 1. In the desktop app, no failure is ever reported, and a thrown one reaches OrcaSlicer's generic handler
22	- **Where:**
23	  - The entry-point handler is `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:926-947` (`on_page_message`). It catches `json::exception`, adds the message type and id, and rethrows. That part is allowed.
24	  - The rethrow, and every other throw from the chat page, the timer pumps, Home's page messages (`Home/HomeHost.cpp:161`), Home's `CallAfter` bodies (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:749`, `:769-785`, `:851-863`, `:1371-1378`) and the tool pump (`ShellController.cpp:337-339`, which has no try), all end in `GUI_App::OnExceptionInMainLoop` → `generic_exception_handle` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:855-909`, `:9600-9604`).
25	  - Nothing in Agent/ or Home/ calls a reporting function.
26	- **What the code does:** OrcaSlicer's handler writes a log line and queues `wxLogError("OrcaSlicer got an unhandled exception: %1%")` with the exception text, then rethrows with `throw;`. The comment at `AgentHost.cpp:931-934` says this handler "logs it and reports it once". It does not report.
27	- **Rule broken:** "One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports."
28	- **What goes wrong:** Someone hits a bug, for example a page message missing a field, or Home asking for an unknown sign-in link (`OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:740`). They see an Orca-branded error that holds internal text such as "jusprin-agent-bridge: … ". Nothing reaches JusPrin. My inference, not run: because the handler rethrows, the app then quits.
29	- **Confidence:** high for the missing handler and report. Medium that the app quits.
30	- **Confirmed:** yes.
31	
32	### 2. A model list whose shape changes crashes the app, because parsing throws on OrcaSlicer's HTTP thread
33	- **Where:**
34	  - `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:43-62`: `on_complete` calls `parse_model_list`.
35	  - `Agent/ModelCatalog.cpp:177-188`: it reads `response.at("data")`, `model.at("id").get<std::string>()`, `model.at("format")` and `model.at("credits").get<int>()`.
36	  - `src/slic3r/Utils/Http.cpp:796-801`: `perform()` runs `http_perform` on a `std::thread`. At `:519-526` that thread calls `completefn` directly, with no try around it.
37	- **What the code does:** If one model entry has no `format`, or its `credits` is not an integer, a `json` exception leaves a `std::thread` body. That calls `std::terminate`.
38	- **Rule broken:** "One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure…". The HTTP callback is an entry point with no handler. Keeping the parser strict is right; what is missing is the handler at the top.
39	- **What goes wrong:** One field changed on JusPrin Cloud, or in a provider's model list, makes the app quit each time it fetches models. That happens at launch and at sign-in. Nothing is reported.
40	- **Confidence:** high, by reading.
41	- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).
42	
43	### 3. An AI-request status the table does not name is shown as a network problem, and every 5xx as "temporarily unavailable"
44	- **Where:** `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:667-699` (`http_error`).
45	- **What the code does:** It sorts statuses by fixed rules and ends in `network_error`, "The AI request could not reach the … service.", with Retry. That last line catches:
46	  - 400, 404, 405, 409, 410 and 422;
47	  - 402 from any provider other than JusPrin's account;
48	  - any status other than 408 that came with no curl text.
49	
50	  Any status of 500 or above other than 529 becomes `service_unavailable`. That includes JusPrin Cloud's own 502 `upstream_error` and 500 tracebacks. Because the `>= 500` test comes before the timeout test, the gateway's 504 `timeout` never becomes `timeout`. A 402 from JusPrin Cloud that is not `credits_exhausted` still becomes "You're out of credits." (`:683-685`). 401 and 403 always mean the sign-in ended or the key was rejected (`:673-674`, `:686-687`).
51	- **Rules broken:**
52	  - "A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause."
53	  - "Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it."
54	  - "When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected."
55	- **What goes wrong:**
56	  - JusPrin Cloud refuses the app's own request with 400 `invalid_request`, which is a bug on one of our two ends. The person is told to check their network and Retry, which never helps. Nobody hears of it.
57	  - Someone's OpenAI key cannot use the model they typed, and OpenAI answers 404. They get the same network sentence. Key setup takes the same path (`Agent/AgentSetup.cpp:112-127`).
58	  - A gateway fault reads as a provider outage.
59	- **Confidence:** high.
60	- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

63	- **Where:** `Agent/ResponsesCodec.cpp:176-177` and `Agent/AnthropicCodec.cpp:404-405`. Both turn any `error` or `response.failed` event into `agent_service_error`, "The AI service could not complete the response.", and drop the event's code and message.

65	- **Rules broken:** "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own."
66	- **What goes wrong:** These failures, three of which have table entries, show as the same generic line with Retry:
67	  - Anthropic's mid-stream `overloaded_error` (table: `service_overloaded`);
68	  - the gateway's own mid-stream `timeout` (table: `timeout`);
69	  - the gateway's `upstream_error` (a gateway fault that should be reported).
70	
71	  The saved message keeps only `agent_service_error`.
72	- **Confidence:** high.
73	- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).
74	
75	### 5. Server: a reply that ends with the provider's own error event is recorded as completed, and its chat is kept as completed
76	- **Where:**
77	  - `gateway.py:301-307`: `self.outcome = 'completed'` is set whenever the upstream line iterator ends, whatever the last event was.
78	  - `stream.py:49-52` (Anthropic) and `:67-73` (Responses): an upstream `error` event, or a `response.error`, is rewritten to `STREAM_ERROR_MESSAGE` and forwarded, and the loop carries on.
79	  - `stream.py:100-109`: an unterminated last event is dropped without a word.
80	  - `gateway.py:241`: `keep()` then keeps the chat for fine-tuning as a completed reply.
81	  - `_log` (`gateway.py:330-361`) records outcome `completed` in Langfuse.
82	  - Nothing reports it.
83	- **Rules broken:** "Never record a failure as a success." "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own." (The sentence is "The model service failed while answering.")
84	- **What goes wrong:** When a provider fails mid-reply, the person sees a failure. The Langfuse record says completed. The kept chat, which is training data, holds a failed reply marked as complete. Nobody can count these failures.
85	- **Confidence:** high.
86	- **Confirmed:** yes.
87	
88	### 6. Server: upstream refusals are interpreted and given sentences of their own; only 401, 403 and 404 reach Sentry, and the provider's error text is dropped
89	- **Where:**
90	  - `upstream.py:197-208` (`error_for_status`): 400 and 422 become `invalid_request`, "The model service did not accept the request." Any other 4xx becomes `upstream_error` 502. Every status of 500 or above becomes `unavailable`.
91	  - `gateway.py:320-328` (`_upstream_failed`): Sentry is told only for `is_gateway_fault` statuses (401, 403 and 404, `upstream.py:211-214`). Everything else is `logger.warning`.
92	  - `gateway.py:312-315`: a transport error mid-stream sends an `upstream_error` event. It too is only a warning.
93	  - `gateway.py:321` drops the upstream body on purpose ("an upstream body can echo the prompt"). The client never receives the upstream status.
94	- **Rules broken:**
95	  - "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it."
96	  - "A log line is not a report: it reaches nobody."
97	  - "No other code reports." Sentry is called at the failure site, not in a top handler.
98	- **What goes wrong:** The provider starts refusing the gateway's requests with 400, for example after a model id or field changes. Every person's chat fails, and the app then calls it a network problem (finding 3). The server has only warning lines, with no provider text explaining why.
99	- **Confidence:** high.
100	- **Confirmed:** yes.

103	- **Where:**
104	  - `gateway.py:136-185`: `_handle_in` catches only `GatewayError`. Anything else leaves `GatewayEndpoint.asgi` (`:117-130`) for daphne.
